implementation_notes: Scala's implicits can hide the provider choice from the entire codebase, which is convenient until you want to change it — then the implicit resolution graph has to be unwound. The safe shape is the explicit one: a type class or a plain trait for the capability, the provider implementation in an adapter object, and the binding at the composition root. Vendor-specific Scala libraries (an S3 client's types, a database driver's row types) must not appear in case classes used outside the adapter, because case class constructors are part of your API.
idiom_name: provider types in case classes; implicits that hide the choice
pitfalls: An `implicit val` for the provider client makes the dependency invisible to `grep -r import`, so the audit misses it.
Case class fields of vendor types leak the provider through every copy() call and every serialiser.
Third-party Scala libraries that wrap AWS/GCP types commonly re-export them, so a dependency on the library is also a dependency on the provider.
